title: Malformed WebSocket Response frame yields Unknown, not a transport error
description: In ws/mod.rs parse_ws_frame(), when the @type is 'Response' but the JSON cannot be deserialized as JmapResponse, the function returns Ok(WsFrame::Unknown) rather than Err(ClientError::Parse). The code comment states the reason: 'A malformed Response frame must not kill the entire WebSocket connection; only tungstenite transport errors warrant a reconnect.' A contributor might argue that returning an error is 'stricter' or 'more visible'. But a strict error here would force the caller to reconnect and re-subscribe, losing buffered events, over what might be a single server-side bug in one response frame. RFC 8887 §4.3.1 instructs clients to ignore unknown message types. The same principle applies to malformed known types: degrade gracefully. Do not change this to return Err.
